dedupe_keys.name: fresnelpath terrain aware rf planning software

description: FresnelPath is a web-based terrain-aware RF planning platform for point-to-point links, area coverage, LoRaWAN, Wi-Fi HaLow and low-Earth-orbit satellite IoT. The site lists six propagation models with automatic routing (free-space, Okumura-Hata, COST-231, ITM, ITWOM 3.0 and ITU-R P.1812-6), four-method knife-edge diffraction (P.526-15), 60 percent Fresnel zone clearance, an asymmetric link budget with fade margin and snow and ice attenuation (P.840-8), 30 m GLO-30 terrain in 3D, multi-gateway coverage heatmaps with best-server and viewshed, ITU-R P.1546-6 regional sweeps, LoRaWAN dimensioning for spreading factors SF7 to SF12 with 12 regional plans, interference planning by graph colouring and solar viability with PVGIS for remote sites. Producer: FresnelPath; the company reports 30 to 40 percent of IoT deployments need unplanned re-siting, a claim not verified here. Coverage: global, wherever terrain and propagation inputs are available. Access: a hosted service with free RF calculators and a planning workflow (define, analyse, decide, publish). Licence and cost: commercial; pricing was not read, so cost is recorded as on request. Caveats: closed-source, and the accuracy figures shown are vendor examples. Simulation uses: link feasibility and coverage planning for wireless networks and remote sensor deployments. Related records: RadioPlanner (platform-radioplanner) and the Py1812 implementation (model-py1812).
